'''Jonathan Brice Johnson''' (born June 27, 1994) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Nelson Giants]] of the New Zealand [[National Basketball League (New Zealand)|National Basketball League]] (NZNBL). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina Tar Heels]], graduating in 2016. He was selected in the first round (25th pick overall) by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in the [[2016 NBA draft]].

==Early life==
Johnson is a native of [[Orangeburg, South Carolina]] and attended Edisto High School, where his father was the varsity basketball coach. Johnson's mother, Renee Johnson, died from colon cancer when he was a teenager.<ref>{{cite web|title=Brice Johnson remembers his momma's love every time he puts on his jersey|url=http://www.dailytarheel.com/article/2016/02/brice-johnson-remembers-his-mommas-love-every-time-he-puts-on-his-jersey|access-date=17 May 2016|work=[[The Daily Tar Heel]]|date=17 February 2016}}</ref>

==College career==
As a sophomore, Johnson averaged 10.3 points and 6.1 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite web|title=Brice Johnson Stats|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/brice-johnson-1.html|access-date=12 May 2016|work=[[Sports Reference]]|date=8 March 2015}}</ref>
As a junior, Johnson was named third-team All-ACC after averaging 12.6 points and 7.8 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite web|title=ACSMA 2015 All-ACC Basketball Teams Announced|url=http://www.theacc.com/news/acsma-all-acc-basketball-teams-announced-03-08-2015|access-date=29 April 2015|work=[[Atlantic Coast Conference]]|date=8 March 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150425010314/http://www.theacc.com/news/acsma-all-acc-basketball-teams-announced-03-08-2015|archive-date=25 April 2015}}</ref><ref name="Carter">{{cite news|url=http://www.newsobserver.com/sports/college/acc/unc/article68146492.html|title=From quitter to All-American: The odyssey of UNC's Brice Johnson |last=Carter|first=Andrew|date=March 24, 2016|work=[[The News & Observer]]|access-date=25 March 2016}}</ref>

Johnson's senior season proved to be his most impressive and he collected many accolades.  As a senior co-captain, Johnson led the Tar Heels to the outright ACC regular season title, as well as the ACC tournament championship. On January 4, 2016, Johnson scored 39 points and collected 23 rebounds in leading the Tar Heels in a victory over [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]] 106–90. He became the second North Carolina player in its history to score at least 39 points and grab 23 rebounds in a single game, after [[Billy Cunningham]] achieved the feat twice in 1964.<ref>{{cite news|title=Brice Johnson scores 39 to lead No. 7 UNC past Florida State|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2016/01/04/johnson-scores-39-to-lead-no-6-unc-past-florida-state/78286118/|access-date=5 January 2016|work=[[USA Today]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=4 January 2016}}</ref> He was named to the 35-man midseason watchlist for the [[Naismith College Player of the Year|Naismith Trophy]] on February 11.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Payne|first1=Terrence|title=Naismith Trophy midseason list announced|url=http://www.foxsports.com/college-basketball/story/oklahoma-sooners-buddy-hield-lsu-tigers-ben-simmons-naismith-trophy-35-finalists-021116|access-date=February 19, 2016|work=[[Fox Sports]]|date=February 11, 2016}}</ref>  On March 27, 2016, Johnson set a new North Carolina school record for most double-doubles in a season.  He also tied the North Carolina school record for most rebounds in a season with 399, matching [[Tyler Hansbrough]]'s 2008 season. On March 29, 2016, Johnson was unanimously selected to the Associated Press' 2015–16 All-America team.<ref>{{cite news|title=UNC's Brice Johnson makes AP All-America team |url=http://abc11.com/sports/uncs-brice-johnson-makes-ap-all-america-team/1267655/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160401003836/http://abc11.com/sports/uncs-brice-johnson-makes-ap-all-america-team/1267655/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 1, 2016 |access-date=March 30, 2016 |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=March 29, 2016 }}</ref>  Johnson finished the 2015–2016 college basketball season with 416 rebounds, setting a new UNC record for most rebounds in a season, passing Tyler Hansbrough. Brice Johnson playing some of his best basketball in college led the Tar Heels with Marcus Paige to the NCAA men's basketball championship game where they fell short to Villanova 77–74 where he put up 14 points and had 8 rebounds.

==Professional career==

===Los Angeles Clippers (2016–2018)===
On June 23, 2016, Johnson was selected by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] with the 25th overall pick in the [[2016 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/nba/2016/06/23/brice-johnson-2016-nba-draft|title=Clippers select Brice Johnson with No. 25 pick of 2016 NBA draft|work=SI.com|date=June 23, 2016|access-date=June 23, 2016}}</ref> On July 12, 2016, he signed his rookie scale contract with the Clippers.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/clippers-sign-brice-johnson|title=L.A. CLIPPERS SIGN BRICE JOHNSON|work=NBA.com|date=July 12, 2016|access-date=July 12, 2016}}</ref> On October 8, 2016, he was ruled out indefinitely due to a herniated disk in his lower back.<ref>{{cite web|last=Turner|first=Broderick|url=http://www.latimes.com/la-sp-clippers-brice-johnson--20161008-snap-story.html|title=Clippers rookie Brice Johnson out indefinitely because of herniated disk in lower back|work=[[Los Angeles Times]]|date=October 8, 2016|access-date=October 8, 2016}}</ref> On February 23, 2017, he made his professional debut in a 123–113 loss to the [[Golden State Warriors]], recording two rebounds in two minutes off the bench. During his rookie season, Johnson had multiple assignments to the [[Salt Lake City Stars]] of the [[NBA Development League]], pursuant to the flexible assignment rule.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/assignments/|title=2016–17 NBA Assignments|work=NBA.com|access-date=March 9, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170126075350/http://dleague.nba.com/assignments/|archive-date=January 26, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> On April 10, 2017, he recorded his first 2 points in a 125–96 win over the Houston Rockets.

===Memphis Grizzlies (2018)===
On January 29, 2018, Johnson, along with [[Willie Reed]] and [[Blake Griffin]], was traded to the [[Detroit Pistons]] in exchange for [[Avery Bradley]], [[Tobias Harris]], [[Boban Marjanović]], a future protected first-round draft pick and a future second-round draft pick.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/press-release-clippers-acquire-harris-bradley-marjanovic|title=Press Release: L.A. Clippers Acquire Harris, Bradley, Marjanović, First & Second-Round Picks|work=NBA.com|date=January 29, 2018|access-date=January 30, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2018/01/30/detroit-pistons-acquire-griffin-harris-bradley-marjanovic-release|title=Detroit Pistons acquire Blake Griffin, Willie Reed, Brice Johnson from LA Clippers|work=NBA.com|date=January 30, 2018|access-date=January 30, 2018}}</ref> On February 8, the Pistons traded Johnson, along with a 2022 second-round draft pick, to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in exchange for [[James Ennis (basketball)|James Ennis]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-acquire-forward-james-ennis-iii | title=Detroit Pistons Acquire Forward James Ennis III |work=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. |date=February 8, 2018 |access-date=February 8, 2018}}</ref> On March 27, 2018, Johnson was waived by the Grizzlies.<ref>{{cite web|title=Memphis Grizzlies sign MarShon Brooks to 10-day contract Grizzlies Waive Brice Johnson|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-sign-marshon-brooks-to-10-day-contract-180327|date=March 27, 2018|work=NBA.com|access-date=March 27, 2018}}</ref>

===Indios de Mayagüez (2019)===
On February 19, 2019, [[Indios de Mayagüez (basketball)|Indios de Mayagüez]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]] (BSN) announced that they had signed Johnson.<ref>{{cite web|title=Indios anuncian a Johnson como su segundo importado|language=ES|url=https://www.bsnpr.com/noticias/detalles.asp?r=+18539|date=February 19, 2019|website=bsnpr.com|access-date=February 19, 2019}}</ref>

===Orlandina (2019–2020)===
On August 14, 2019, Johnson signed with [[Orlandina Basket]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/brice-johnson-joins-orlandina-basket/|title=Brice Johnson joins Orlandina Basket|newspaper=Sportando |date=14 August 2019 |access-date=14 August 2019|last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }}</ref> He averaged 17 points and 11 rebounds per game.<ref name="Budivelnyk" />

===Chorale Roanne Basket (2020)===
On January 11, 2020, Johnson signed with [[Chorale Roanne Basket]] of the [[LNB Pro A]], a professional basketball league in France.<ref>{{cite news |title=Brice Johnson joins Chorale Roanne |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/brice-johnson-joins-chorale-roanne/ |website=Sportando |access-date=October 7, 2020 |date=January 11, 2020|last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }}</ref> He averaged 13 points and five rebounds per game.<ref name="Budivelnyk" />

===BC Budivelnyk (2020–2021)===
On October 7, 2020, Johnson signed with [[BC Budivelnyk]] of the [[Ukrainian Basketball SuperLeague]].<ref name="Budivelnyk">{{cite news |title=BC Budivelnyk sign Brice Johnson, Reggie Johnson |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/bc-budivelnyk-sign-brice-johnson-reggie-johnson/ |website=Sportando |access-date=October 7, 2020 |date=October 7, 2020|last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }}</ref> He averaged 13 points, 8.4 rebounds, 1.5 blocks and 1.2 steals per game.<ref name="hughes" />

===Toyama Grouses (2021–2023)===
On July 8, 2021, Johnson signed with the [[Toyama Grouses]] of the [[B.League]].<ref name="hughes">{{cite web |last1=Hughes |first1=Grant |title=Brice Johnson Signs to Play in Japan |url=https://247sports.com/college/north-carolina/Article/Brice-Johnson-Toyama-Grouses-B-League-of-Japan-UNC-Basketball-167460895/ |website=247 Sports |access-date=July 6, 2021 |date=July 6, 2021}}</ref> He played two seasons for the Grouses.<ref name=Eurobasket>{{cite web |title=Brice Johnson, Basketball Player, News, Stats - australiabasket |url=https://basketball.australiabasket.com/player/Brice-Johnson/263875 |website=Eurobasket LLC |access-date=12 February 2025 |url-access=subscription}}</ref>

===Al-Seeb (2023)===
Johnson played for Omani club [[Al-Seeb Club]] during the [[2023 Arab Club Basketball Championship]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Al Seeb signs Brice Johnson, ex Toyama G. |url=https://www.asia-basket.com/Oman/news/830502/Al-Seeb-signs-Brice-Johnson-ex-Toyama-G |access-date=12 February 2025 |work=asia-basket.com |date=3 October 2023}}</ref> In five games, he averaged 23.0 points, 8.8 rebounds, 1.8 assists and 2.0 steals per game.<ref name="Eurobasket" />

===Nelson Giants (2025)===
In February 2025, Johnson signed with the [[Nelson Giants]] of the New Zealand [[National Basketball League (New Zealand)|National Basketball League]] (NZNBL) for the [[2025 New Zealand NBL season|2025 season]].<ref>{{cite news |title=BRICE JOHNSON SIGNED FOR 2025 |url=https://www.facebook.com/nelsongiants/posts/pfbid022QmBHK7NDLgDCkVZUf3XHDvbn6wCgsxt5NJvwE7CHd4HA1sB93aFsUFJYxuzuToZl |access-date=12 February 2025 |work=facebook.com/nelsongiants |date=12 February 2025}}</ref> On April 16, 2025, he was released by the Giants.<ref>{{cite news |title=The NBS Nelson Giants have made the difficult decision to release import forward Brice Johnson, effective immediately. |url=https://www.facebook.com/nelsongiants/posts/pfbid02Qt7PMEa2Dcj3MYwgjJXpM1RBJKK5w3hZBJF9n7rEFqEp5k6rr4bXjef17QMf9P53l |access-date=16 April 2025 |work=facebook.com/nelsongiants |date=16 April 2025}}</ref>
